rq: joint identification of raw language equivalence and latent intervention partition

Hu et al., An Information Theoretic Approach to Interaction-Grounded Learning, ICML 2024

decision: NARROWED BEYOND INTERACTION-GROUNDED LATENT-REWARD IDENTIFIABILITY — NOT ADOPTED
reason: IGL already identifies a useful latent binary reward decoder and high-value policy from unlabelled interaction feedback under conditional independence and a sufficiently bad baseline-policy orientation anchor. This guarantee identifies reward-relevant grounding, not an unknown raw-utterance equivalence relation, a latent semantic intervention-target partition, or a unique denotation. Joint utterance/target recodings and semantic refinements inside reward-and-feedback-equivalent blocks preserve the complete interactive law.
surviving_candidate: After recovering the strongest non-language causal target partition and the finest reward/feedback-equivalence partition identifiable from all legitimate interactions, determine whether a preregistered raw-language law uniquely separates only the remaining reward-and-intervention-aliased blocks and jointly identifies utterance equivalence, residual semantic target partition, and denotation while eliminating every joint utterance/target/reward-decoder/policy recoding preserving the complete interactive law.
public_baseline_reproduction: not started; no paper-specific official implementation located
